doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: Rides to gigs and the drinking he saw, including Jaski's amp
summary: Palmer and parents drove him to gigs. He saw heavy drinking, including Jaski's pill bottles of Manhattans in an amp, and found the rock musicians unprofessional.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Who took you to the gigs when you were 15?

My parents sometimes, sometimes the people that would hire me. Jack Palmer, the first gig I can remember the trip with him, he came and picked me up and I wish I could tell you that story but unfortunately I can’t. But after Romy leaves and we’re alone, I’ll tell you the first thing he ever said to me in the car on the way to a gig, which is very funny but —
Okay, that’s for part two which will be inaccessible.
Did you see things — I could ask it this way. Did you see behavior on gigs that you had to make a judgement about. Am I going to choose to drink like this person, and all that kind of stuff?

Yeah, sure. John Jaski, go back to him, he would give me an amp to take to a gig. And I remember once taking an amp and as I’m taking it in there was a rattling like crazy and I thought oh my God, the tubes came out, I broke some tubes in his amp. And when I got there I looked in the back of the amp and there were all these pill bottles filled with — he used to make Manhattans at home and fill up these pill bottles with them, and so during the gig he would just reach back into the amp and bango. So everybody — there was a lot of heavy drinking in musicians. Some of the behaviors, actually it was later on when I played with rock groups and I thought man you guys are so unprofessional. It was crazy, because I was always with the adults you know. So there was a certain kind of way you © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-
presented yourself. And when I saw that kind of amateurish — with people that I was playing with — it was a little disturbing.
